stem: Plants in one bench wilt despite moist media. The containers drain slowly and roots in affected pots appear poorly aerated. Which next step best supports the differential?
choices: Evaluate physical structure, drainage, aeration, moisture distribution, and root condition before assuming the plants simply need more irrigation.
Increase irrigation frequency because wilting always means the media are too dry.
Ignore root observations because above-ground symptoms determine the diagnosis.
Raise nutrient concentration before checking drainage or aeration.
rationale: Wilting can occur when root-zone physical or aeration constraints impair water uptake even when media are wet; the next step should discriminate among physical, moisture, and chemical constraints.
